lesson.title: 911 Intake Basics (Greeting, Location, Professionalism)
objectives: Apply professional calltaker language (avoid prohibited phrasing).
Know what identifying info may/must be provided when requested.

questions.stem: What is the required greeting when answering a NYC 911 call?

choices.text: NYC emergency services, what do you want?
New York City 911, do you need Police, Fire or Medical?

questions.solution: The guide requires the greeting to be stated verbatim.

questions.stem: At the end of every call, what statement is the calltaker required to say (including operator number)?

choices.text: Assistance will be provided as soon as possible, Operator #____
Police are on the way immediately.
Call back if it gets worse.

questions.solution: The guide requires the operator number be stated at the end of every call.

questions.stem: Calltakers should always ask the caller what two streets the address is between to verify the location.
Using slang (e.g., 'yo', 'bro') is acceptable if it calms the caller down.
Always ask the caller: “What two __________ are you between?”
A crime is entered as 'in the past' when it occurred __________ minutes or more ago (and the perpetrator is not still in the immediate area).
Which option is MOST consistent with the guide’s professionalism approach?

choices.text: Tell the caller to stop yelling or you won’t help.
Use calm, respectful terms of address like sir/madam and avoid escalating.
Use sarcasm to show the caller they’re wrong.
Use police jargon so the caller knows you’re serious.

questions.solution: The guide emphasizes tact, restraint, and respectful address; avoid escalating language.

questions.stem: Which is part of the normal order/requirement for eliciting location information?

choices.text: Get apartment/floor details and include them with the address entry.
Skip the address until you fully understand the story.
Only enter cross streets—street address is optional.
Tell the caller the address is invalid if it doesn’t verify.

questions.solution: The guide emphasizes capturing address details (including apt/floor) and not telling callers the address is 'not valid'.

questions.stem: Match each item to the best reason it matters.
answer: Standardized opening that must be stated verbatim
Improves response accuracy within a building
Helps classify crimes as 'past' based on time
